svg.text: Human-in-the-Loop — when the system stops and asks, and what happens next
Escalation is a designed path, not an error. The graph pauses at a checkpoint, a human decides, the graph resumes. Nothing is lost while waiting.
TRIGGERS (any one fires)
Planner confidence below threshold
e.g. plan_confidence < 0.6, or plan has unresolved ambiguity
Sensitive tool call
send email · payment · delete · external write (gate says risky/destructive)
Specialist failed twice on the same subtask
reviewer rejected 2×, or tool errors exhausted retries
Reviewer quality score below threshold
final deliverable scored < 3/5 by the reviewer
User asked for review
request flag: require_human_review = true
Escalation router
trigger → level (policy table,
configurable per deployment)
LEVELS (how much the human does)
L1 · Notify
proceed, but post to Slack/UI. Human can intervene later.
use: low-confidence plan on a low-stakes task
L2 · Approve action
pause before ONE tool call; human confirms or rejects it.
use: risky/destructive tool calls
L3 · Approve plan
pause before ANY work; human edits/approves the full plan.
use: low confidence + high stakes, or user requested
L4 · Take over
agents stop; human supplies the output directly.
use: repeated failure, or reviewer score very low
APPROVAL QUEUE → REVIEW UI
What the graph does when it escalates
1. interrupt() — node returns, checkpointer writes TaskState to Postgres
2. insert approvals row: task_id, level, trigger, proposed_action, reasoning
3. notify: Slack webhook + UI badge; API status = "awaiting_approval"
4. the worker moves on to other tasks — nothing blocks
What the reviewer sees (context package)
• original request · the plan · steps already done (with outputs)
• the exact decision point: proposed action + the agent's reasoning
• similar past decisions from tier-3 memory ("last time you said…")
• a chat panel to ask the agent "why?" before deciding
Timeout policy
No decision in N hours → default per level (L1 nothing, L2 deny the action,
L3/L4 cancel task). Never auto-approve on timeout.
THE FOUR DECISIONS AND HOW THE GRAPH RESUMES
Approve
POST /approvals/{id}/decide {approve}
→ graph.invoke(Command(resume="approve"))
→ the paused node continues exactly where it
stopped; the tool executes / plan proceeds
Modify
human edits the plan or the tool arguments
→ Command(resume={edited...})
→ state updated, then continues. The edit is
logged and becomes a tier-3 memory
Reject (with reason)
→ Command(resume={reject, reason})
→ for a tool call: model gets an error
tool_result and re-plans that step
→ for a plan: back to plan node with feedback
Take over
human types the deliverable themselves
→ Command(goto="deliver", update={final_output})
→ agents skipped; human output is stored with a
"human_authored" flag and used as a training example
NUMBERS TO TRACK (these go on the resume)
• Escalation rate — % of tasks that needed a human, by trigger and by level. Falling over time = the system is learning.
• Approval rate — of escalations, how many were approved unchanged? High = triggers are too sensitive. Low = the agent proposes bad actions.
• Time-to-decision — how long tasks sit in the queue. Drives the timeout policy.
• Blocked-destructive count — how many destructive actions the gate stopped. "Zero unapproved external actions across N tasks" is a strong headline.
• Human-corrected outputs — every Modify/Take-over is a labelled example for the eval set (the Project 13 flywheel, for free).
